dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Rustam, did you see Professor Aidarov after the lecture? I heard he spoke to you.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Yes — he stopped me in the corridor. He said he'd enjoyed my question about purism.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I asked him whether he thought language purism was possible in a globalised world. He said it probably wasn't, but that the impulse behind it was understandable.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That's interesting. Did he say anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: He told me to come to his office hours if I wanted to discuss it more. He said he was researching the same topic for a new paper.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I think so. He also mentioned that the linguistics department was looking for student research assistants next semester.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Really? Did he say what they would be working on?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: He said they would be helping with a project on language contact in western Kazakhstan. He asked whether any of us were interested.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Did he say who to contact if we were?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: He told me to email Dr Serikova in the research office. He said the deadline for applications was the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That's soon. I'm going to apply. I love the idea of research on Kazakh language contact.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Me too. He told me the positions were competitive but that student applications were very welcome.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: What did he say about the selection criteria?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: He said they were looking for students with curiosity and commitment — not necessarily those with the highest grades.
